investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-17T01:44–01:52Z because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler: only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both reported insufficient capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected for any check, confirming the agent VM never reached a schedulable state.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm peer-pod VM slots on the 2 nodes that carry that resource. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" and the identical failure across all three sibling checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) confirm that no new remote-agent pod can be placed. Preemption was also ruled out ("No preemption victims found"), meaning no lower-priority pods exist to evict. The eval never advanced past pod scheduling, so all required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) remained empty. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
proof: failed-check.message: scheduler reports '0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.' — pod stuck unscheduled for 124s.
failed-check.timing: status=fail latencyMs=130709, eval timed out well before the outageLatencyMs threshold of 360000ms, confirming the pod never became schedulable within the probe window.
failed-check.evidence: evidence object is empty — no orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, or remoteState was captured, consistent with the agent VM never starting.

expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all 4 required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are missing, matching the contract defined at infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json line 256.
sibling.remote-agent-state: identical scheduler error, pod stuck for 143s, no evidence collected.
sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical scheduler error, pod stuck for 146s, no evidence collected.

source.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1885: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) — the remote agent pod creation is the first blocking step; if it cannot be scheduled, no downstream evidence is ever written.
possibleCauses: [Most likely] kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots are fully consumed on both eligible nodes — all in-flight or running remote-agent pods have claimed the available VM quota, leaving zero capacity for new pods. Preemption being unhelpful confirms no lower-priority pods are present to reclaim slots.

[Possible] The 4 non-kata nodes have a node affinity or node selector mismatch (e.g., a label such as kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable or a runtime class selector) that permanently excludes them from scheduling remote-agent pods, concentrating all scheduling pressure on only 2 nodes and making the cluster more susceptible to exhaustion.

[Possible] A prior eval run or a leaked remote-agent pod from a previous probe cycle was not cleaned up (withCleanup in run-status-probes.mjs is responsible for teardown), leaving VM slots occupied and unavailable for the current run.
[Less likely] A cluster scaling event reduced the number of kata-capable nodes from a previously higher count to 2, shrinking available VM capacity without a corresponding reduction in demand.

investigation.title: Remote Agent Pods Unschedulable Due to Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity — All Three Remote-Agent Checks Failing
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod created by the eval runner was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler with "Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm" on the 2 nodes that support peer-pod VMs, while the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because no pod could be scheduled, the createAgent call in run-status-probes.mjs never completed, and the eval produced zero evidence — leaving all four required fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) missing from the contract.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent feature has exhausted the schedulable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry that resource. With 0 available VM slots and no preemption victims, every new remote-agent pod is stuck Unschedulable. This prevents the eval runner's createAgent call (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs, line 1905) from producing an agent, so the probe times out without writing any evidence, causing the remote-agent-state contract validation to fail with all four required fields missing. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: all available VM slots are consumed by existing workloads, leaving no capacity for new eval-created remote-agent pods. Supported directly by the scheduler message in failed-check.message and both sibling check messages.

Secondary — node affinity/selector mismatch on the remaining 4 nodes: the remote-agent pod spec requires a node label or taint that only the 2 kata.peerpods nodes carry, so even if VM slots were freed on other nodes, those nodes would still be ineligible. This is a structural constraint, not a transient one.

Tertiary — a prior eval run or production workload may have left remote-agent pods running and not cleaned up, consuming the finite VM slots. The withCleanup wrapper in run-status-probes.mjs (line 1903) is intended to handle cleanup, but if a previous run crashed before cleanup, leaked pods could hold slots.

Because the agent pod never became schedulable, the eval runner's createAgent call never returned a live agent, so zero evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) were collected and the expected-output contract was entirely unmet.

With 0/6 nodes available and preemption unable to free capacity, every pod submitted by the eval runner (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) was stuck Unschedulable for 124–146 seconds before the eval timed out. This is a cluster-level resource exhaustion condition localized to the kata PeerPods VM resource pool, not a code defect in the eval runner or contract definitions. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the evidence; this is an eval-infrastructure failure against the production-api environment.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-17T01:44–01:52Z because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler: only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both reported insufficient capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected for any check, confirming the agent VM never reached a schedulable state.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm peer-pod VM slots on the 2 nodes that carry that resource. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" and the identical failure across all three sibling checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) confirm that no new remote-agent pod can be placed. Preemption was also ruled out ("No preemption victims found"), meaning no lower-priority pods exist to evict. The eval never advanced past pod scheduling, so all required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) remained empty. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
proof: failed-check.message: scheduler reports '0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.' — pod stuck unscheduled for 124s.
failed-check.timing: status=fail latencyMs=130709, eval timed out well before the outageLatencyMs threshold of 360000ms, confirming the pod never became schedulable within the probe window.
failed-check.evidence: evidence object is empty — no orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, or remoteState was captured, consistent with the agent VM never starting.

expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all 4 required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are missing, matching the contract defined at infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json line 256.
sibling.remote-agent-state: identical scheduler error, pod stuck for 143s, no evidence collected.
sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical scheduler error, pod stuck for 146s, no evidence collected.

source.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1885: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) — the remote agent pod creation is the first blocking step; if it cannot be scheduled, no downstream evidence is ever written.
possibleCauses: [Most likely] kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots are fully consumed on both eligible nodes — all in-flight or running remote-agent pods have claimed the available VM quota, leaving zero capacity for new pods. Preemption being unhelpful confirms no lower-priority pods are present to reclaim slots.

[Possible] The 4 non-kata nodes have a node affinity or node selector mismatch (e.g., a label such as kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable or a runtime class selector) that permanently excludes them from scheduling remote-agent pods, concentrating all scheduling pressure on only 2 nodes and making the cluster more susceptible to exhaustion.

[Possible] A prior eval run or a leaked remote-agent pod from a previous probe cycle was not cleaned up (withCleanup in run-status-probes.mjs is responsible for teardown), leaving VM slots occupied and unavailable for the current run.
[Less likely] A cluster scaling event reduced the number of kata-capable nodes from a previously higher count to 2, shrinking available VM capacity without a corresponding reduction in demand.

investigations.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod created by the eval runner was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler with "Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm" on the 2 nodes that support peer-pod VMs, while the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because no pod could be scheduled, the createAgent call in run-status-probes.mjs never completed, and the eval produced zero evidence — leaving all four required fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) missing from the contract.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent feature has exhausted the schedulable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry that resource. With 0 available VM slots and no preemption victims, every new remote-agent pod is stuck Unschedulable. This prevents the eval runner's createAgent call (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs, line 1905) from producing an agent, so the probe times out without writing any evidence, causing the remote-agent-state contract validation to fail with all four required fields missing. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Eval Failure: Kubernetes Kata PeerPods VM Capacity Exhausted — All Three Remote-Agent Checks Unschedulable
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because the Kubernetes scheduler could not place the required kata.peerpods.io VM pods: only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both reported insufficient capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. Because the agent pod never became schedulable, the eval runner's createAgent call never returned a live agent, so zero evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) were collected and the expected-output contract was entirely unmet.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent swarm has exhausted the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry it. With 0/6 nodes available and preemption unable to free capacity, every pod submitted by the eval runner (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) was stuck Unschedulable for 124–146 seconds before the eval timed out. This is a cluster-level resource exhaustion condition localized to the kata PeerPods VM resource pool, not a code defect in the eval runner or contract definitions. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the evidence; this is an eval-infrastructure failure against the production-api environment.

possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource pool exhausted on the 2 eligible nodes: concurrent workloads or prior eval runs consumed all available VM slots, leaving no capacity for new eval pods. Supported by all three sibling checks reporting the same Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm message.

SECONDARY — Node affinity or node selector on the remote-agent pod spec restricts scheduling to only the 2 kata-capable nodes, and those nodes are at capacity. The 4 remaining nodes are structurally ineligible (wrong labels/taints), so the cluster has no fallback. Supported by '4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector' in failed-check.message.

TERTIARY — The kata PeerPods node pool may be undersized for the current eval concurrency: all three checks ran sequentially within a ~5-minute window (01:47–01:52Z) and each required its own VM pod, potentially stacking against a small fixed pool.

affectedAreas.label: Kubernetes kata PeerPods VM resource pool (production-api cluster)
affectedAreas.reason: The scheduler message 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' on both eligible nodes is the direct cause of all three eval pod failures. This is the earliest violated boundary in the failure chain.

affectedAreas.label: Remote agent pod node affinity / node selector configuration

recommendedNextActions: Immediately check the production-api Kubernetes cluster for kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes. If all slots are consumed, identify and terminate any stale or leaked eval pods to restore capacity.
Re-run the three remote-agent eval checks after confirming or restoring VM slot availability to determine whether the failure is resolved by capacity recovery alone.

Assess whether the kata PeerPods node pool is sized appropriately for the eval concurrency pattern. If all three remote-agent checks each require a dedicated VM pod and run within the same workflow window, the pool needs at least 3 concurrent VM slots.

Consider adding a pre-flight check in the eval runner that queries available kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity before attempting agent creation, and returns a SKIP or WARN status with a descriptive message instead of waiting for a scheduling timeout.
Add a follow-up eval or cluster health check that monitors kata.peerpods.io/vm utilization and alerts when available slots fall below the minimum required for the remote-agent eval suite.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl or cluster metrics show that kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity was available and unused on the 2 eligible nodes at the time of the eval run, the scheduling-exhaustion diagnosis would be disproved and a different cause (e.g., a node taint, quota, or admission webhook rejection) would need to be investigated.

If the remote-agent-runtime eval passes on an immediate re-run without any cluster changes, it would suggest the exhaustion was transient (e.g., a competing workload released VM slots) rather than a persistent capacity deficit.

If only remote-agent-runtime failed while remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state passed in a concurrent run, it would suggest the failure is isolated to the runtime probe's pod spec rather than a shared pool exhaustion.

If the pod spec for remote-agent eval pods does not actually request kata.peerpods.io/vm as a resource, the scheduler message would point to a misconfiguration in the pod template rather than true capacity exhaustion.
followUpEvals: Add a dedicated eval check (e.g., remote-agent-vm-capacity) that queries the Kubernetes API for available kata.peerpods.io/vm slots and fails or warns when capacity is below the minimum needed for the remote-agent eval suite, providing early warning before scheduling failures occur.

Add a stale-pod detection eval that lists pods requesting kata.peerpods.io/vm older than a configurable threshold and fails if any are found, catching cleanup regressions before they exhaust the pool.

Extend the remote-agent-create check to emit a structured scheduling-failure evidence field (e.g., schedulingError, unschedulableReason) when the pod cannot be placed, so future investigations have machine-readable signal rather than only a free-text message.

Add a cross-check eval that verifies all three remote-agent checks (create, state, runtime) pass within a single run window, catching cases where sequential pod requests exhaust a small VM pool even if individual checks would pass in isolation.
